xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheAuthority: Senior Inspector, Legal Metrology, Mahoba, UP
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NatureAndDetailsOfTheActionTak: Compounding fee of INR 50,000 under Legal Metrology Act 2009
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Package containing Microfibre cloth did not contain the Legal Metrology mandatory declaration of ‘dimension of the product’ i.e. the size of cloth in cm.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: There is no major impact on financial, operation or other activities of the Company.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: The Company has received an Adjudication order dated 22nd December 2025 from West Bengal GST Department for the period April 2018 to March 2023 upholding the demand of Rs.0.96 million (Tax Demand-Rs.0.48 million; penalty-Rs.0.48 million) along with the interest, mainly on account of reconciliation of tax returns filed by the Company. Vide the above order, the GST department has also dropped the demand of Rs. 0.32 million.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: Considering small amount, the Company has paid the demand for closure of case. The order will have no major impact on the financial, operation or other activities of the company.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:DetailsOfTheViolationOrContrav: Suzuki Motor Gujarat Private Limited (SMG)- now amalgamated with Maruti Suzuki India Limited (MSIL) has received an Adjudication order dated 23rd December 2025 from Gujarat GST Department for the period April 2018 to March 2019 upholding demand of Rs.0.23 million (Tax demand-Rs.0.07 million, Interest-Rs. 0.09 million and Penalty-Rs.0.07 million) mainly on account of input tax credit issues. Vide the above order, the GST department has also dropped the demand of Rs. 3.36 million.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:ImpactOnFinancialOrOperationOr: The Company is in the process of filing an appeal against the confirmed demand in the adjudication order before the Appellate Authority (similar credit issues being faced by different GST Nos. of MSIL). The order will have no major impact on the financial, operation or other activities of the company.

xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs:
The Company has received an order from the Commissioner of Income Tax Appeal (CIT(A)) for the FY 2009-10 wherein the grounds raised by the Company have been majorly allowed in favour of the Company.
The CIT(A) has deleted key additions amounting to Rs. 3,214 Million and remanded back additions amounting to Rs. 170 Million.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr:
The Company is in process of filing an application before the Assessing Officer to give effect to this order.
Further, for other issues, the Company is in process of filing appeal before the Tribunal.
